column1: # The host-path table of `just affected --narrow` (tools/recipes.py, the section above narrow()).
# glob<TAB>recipes<TAB>why[<TAB>exceptions]. A changed file that some gate reads through a dependency edge (a lib a target links,
# a manifest, a cargo global) selects the recipes of every row whose glob matches it; `*` keeps the full list; no
# row keeps the full list and names the file. A file's own target (its bin, its test file, its lib's own tests), a
# script a recipe names, and the recipe's own text select their recipes without a row, so a row names only the gates
# that reach the file through a dependency; gate-ptx-spill joins a narrowed list only when a scan pair is not identical
# or its own inputs moved (tools/recipes.py, narrow()). `**` crosses `/`, `*` does not,
# `{a,b}` is either. `just check-recipes` holds each row to the tree: its recipes are gate recipes that link every file
# it matches, each alternative matches a file, every gate whose own target names the module the glob stands for is in
# the row, and every gate the derivation says reaches a file the glob matches through another lib is in the row or in
# its exceptions (`python3 tools/recipes.py reach FILE…` prints those gates, each with one chain). The derivation reads
# the item graph of the code (use trees, paths, impls, macros; not docs) from each gate target's own items. The fourth
# column names the gates it reaches that a run-time dispatch keeps off the file: `except gate-… gate-…: reason`
# clauses joined by ` | ` (a serve seat the gate does not open, an Arch arm, a reference-set family it does not read);
# the check counts them in its summary, and an exception naming a gate that does not reach the file is red.
# A data file is read like the items around it: what a target takes by `include_str!`/`include_bytes!` or a path literal
# is a file it reaches, as its own target's (a test's data directory: picked without a row) or through a lib's code (a row,
# as for source). A row whose files only own targets read maps nothing, and the check takes it out.
# Every binary parses the registry and runs at_main first, and a lever's default reaches whoever reads it in place.

column3: the lever table every binary's at_main parses
